findings.summary: assert sum(1 for r in routes.values() if r['source_route']=='lineage') == len(recovered) is not independent of the value under test: `recovered` is built at line ~300 as {sn_id: descendant_sources[r['descendant']] for ... if r['source_route']=='lineage'} from the same `routes` mapping, so the two sides move together and the assertion holds whatever the lineage code does.

assert set(key['case_source_routes']) == {c['sn_id'] for c, _ in contributing} also cannot catch a lineage regression: if the fallback recovered nothing, both the route set and the contributing set shrink together, nothing asserts lineage_recovered_cases > 0, and the gate would still exit 0.

WHERE NOT desc.name_stage IN ['superseded','exhausted'] drops a descendant whose name_stage is NULL (Cypher three-valued logic makes the predicate NULL, which WHERE treats as false), contradicting the stated rule that only superseded/exhausted descendants are skipped; the repository idiom at imas_codex/standard_names/search.py:92 uses coalesce(sn.name_stage,'') for exactly this reason.
